ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.33 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and record the RD-1 breach in the driver's file; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip: the fare record breaks the $49.37 charged into base $3.90 + distance $34.42 for 24.41 km + time $9.58 + platform $1.47, with waiting $0.00 and no surge [F5][F6]. Under RD-2 the metered branch therefore applies and extra kilometres feed the fare, so I apply the per-km rate from this trip's own record rather than any assumed rate [F6][RD-2].

One off-route segment exists: 09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, adding 3.07 km and straying up to 688 m from the optimal route [F3]. RD-1 makes every such segment reviewable under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and no exemption survives: the trace marks RD-4(a) failed (no qualifying incident), and the only road-condition data are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard with fair weather, which does not reach even the band 1/2 support of RD-4(b) [F11][F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. The driver's own brief concedes the same, and his post-trip statement "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is a claim, not a reasonable cause [F10][RD-1].

RD-3 does not apply: the segment contains no measured stop, and the rider never named a place or a road [F3][F7]. RD-5 does not apply either: the chat record is complete and every message is timestamped — the rider's 09:04 pick-up note and the driver's 09:05 arrival note are the only messages, both before the 09:24 segment began, and neither agrees to any route change [F7][F8][F9]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment counts, so the segment stands unexempted [F9][RD-5].

Amount: the distance fare is $34.42 for 24.41 km, giving $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.4101/km [F6]; the unexempted segment's extra_km is 3.07 km [F3]; 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.3290 → $4.33 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The further $0.18 of the $4.51 billed excess-distance line (3.20 km trip-level overshoot priced at the same rate) is corridor/map-matching mileage not attributed to any segment, which RD-2 expressly does not refund [F1][F4][RD-2].

RD-6 is not met: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (his one upheld dispute is on the no-show line), so the repeated-breach predicate for an account flag fails, and profile facts cannot decide the case by themselves [F15][F16][RD-6]. Both advocates eventually requested the same figure, $4.33 [C7][D6].

segment_findings.reason: The off-route segment 09:24–09:30 added 3.07 km [F3]. The chat record is complete with every message timestamped, and the only messages are the rider's 09:04 pick-up note and the driver's 09:05 arrival note — neither agrees to a route change — so no rider message sent before 09:24 agrees to this segment, and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is not consent [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. No rider-named stop exists either, and no RD-4 incident or band 1/2 condition supports a reasonable cause [F13][F11][F12][RD-3][RD-4]. The segment is an unexempted detour and its extra_km are refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 for a flag; the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (the single upheld dispute is on the no-show line), so the repeated-route-dispute predicate fails and an account flag cannot attach [F16][F15][RD-6]. Profile facts cannot decide the case or add a flag on their own [F15][F16][RD-6].

The driver's tenure, trip volume and rating are profile facts and cannot by themselves excuse the segment or decide the case; the finding rests on the unexempted segment and the RD-2 formula [F16][F3][RD-2].

Not rejected on outcome: the driver's concession that no RD-4 exemption applies is accepted — there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch and only band 5 speeds [F13][F11][F12][RD-4] — so the segment remains unexempted and refundable under RD-2, which is the ruling reached here [F3][RD-2].
